title: Boss: lost on a new server
summary: Simulate cd, find and du on a model filesystem.

steps.title: Your first day on prod-7
steps.body: You've been handed SSH access to a server you've never seen. The tests model its filesystem as a list of file paths with sizes, like `find / -type f` would print. Paste your `Resolve` and `Glob` from earlier lessons where you need them.

steps.title: Follow the breadcrumbs
prompt: Write `string AfterCds(string start, List<string> cds, string home)`. Starting at `start`, apply each `cd` argument in order and return the final directory. `"-"` means "the previous directory" (the one you were in before the last `cd`). An empty string means home.
starter: string AfterCds(string start, List<string> cds, string home)
solution: string Resolve(string cwd, string path, string home)
string AfterCds(string start, List<string> cds, string home)
string next = a == "-" ? prev : a == "" ? home : Resolve(cur, a, home);
hints: Keep two variables: current and previous.
`cd -` swaps them: the new previous is the directory you just left.
template: Dojo.Eq("cd - twice toggles", "/etc", AfterCds("/", new List<string> { "/etc", "/tmp", "-", "-", "-" }, "/root"));
Dojo.Eq("bare cd goes home", "/root/x", AfterCds("/srv", new List<string> { "", "x" }, "/root"));

steps.title: find -name
prompt: Write `List<string> Find(List<string> files, string dir, string namePattern)`: every path in `files` that is **under** `dir` (at any depth) and whose **last segment** matches the glob `namePattern`, in the original order. `dir` has no trailing slash, except `/` itself.
Under `/var/log` means the path starts with `/var/log/`. `/var/logs/x` is *not* under `/var/log`.
starter: List<string> Find(List<string> files, string dir, string namePattern)
solution: for (int k = n; k <= name.Length; k++)
if (name[n] >= set[i] && name[n] <= set[i + 2]) hit = true;
List<string> Find(List<string> files, string dir, string namePattern)
hints: Compare against `dir + "/"` so `/var/logs` doesn't count as under `/var/log`.

steps.title: Where did the disk go? (du)
prompt: The disk is full. Write `List<string> TopDirs(List<(string Path, long Bytes)> files, string dir, int n)` that works like `du -s dir/* | sort -rn | head -n`: group every file under `dir` by its **immediate child** of `dir` (a subdirectory or the file itself), sum the bytes, and return the `n` biggest as `"<bytes> <full child path>"`, biggest first; ties by path, alphabetically.
Files directly in `dir` count as their own entry.
starter: List<string> TopDirs(List<(string Path, long Bytes)> files, string dir, int n)
solution: List<string> TopDirs(List<(string Path, long Bytes)> files, string dir, int n)
hints: The child is the first segment of the path after the `dir/` prefix.
GroupBy that child, Sum, OrderByDescending, Take(n).
template: var dojoF = new List<(string Path, long Bytes)> { ("/var/log/syslog", 500), ("/var/log/journal/a", 4000), ("/var/log/journal/b", 3000), ("/var/lib/docker/x", 90000), ("/var/cache/apt/p", 1200), ("/etc/hosts", 10) };
Dojo.Eq("files count as themselves", new List<string> { "7000 /var/log/journal", "500 /var/log/syslog" }, TopDirs(dojoF, "/var/log", 5));
